beats.say: GPS satellite clocks run thirty eight microseconds faster every single day.
Special and general relativity predicted this time difference due to orbital speeds.
The GPS project was started by the United States Department of Defence in 1973.
The prototype spacecraft was successfully launched in 1978 for early testing.
The ultimate constellation of twenty four satellites became fully operational in 1993.
Modern GPS receivers that use the L5 band reach accuracy of thirty centimetres.

facts: Special and general relativity predicted that the clocks on GPS satellites run 38 microseconds faster per day than those on the Earth.
The GPS project was started by the U.S. Department of Defense in 1973.
The prototype spacecraft was launched in 1978 and the ultimate constellation of 24 satellites became operational in 1993.
GPS receivers that use the L5 band have accuracy of 30 centimeters.
